title: Generation of endothelial cells from human-derived iPSCs and integration into mouse brain explants
author: Erzar, Noll, et al.
materials: Mouse anti-alpha smooth muscle actin (αSMA) Cy3

steps.title: Prepare reagents and approvals
steps.instruction: Gather all cell‑culture reagents, sterilize equipment, and verify institutional approvals for human iPSC work and mouse tissue use. Ensure all solutions are prepared under aseptic conditions.

steps.title: Co‑transfect iPSCs with PiggyBac vectors
steps.instruction: Engineer iPSCs to stably express doxycycline‑inducible ETV2 using a PiggyBac transposon system.

substeps.instruction: One day before transfection, split iPSCs and seed 5 × 10⁴ cells per well in a 24‑well plate coated with vitronectin, using Essential 8 (E8) medium only (do not use E8 Flex).
On the day of transfection, replace medium with E8 supplemented with 10 µM Y‑27632 ROCK inhibitor.

Prepare transfection mix: (a) Tube 1 – mix 2 µL Lipofectamine with 25 µL Opti‑MEM; (b) Tube 2 – dissolve 500 ng total plasmid DNA (1:1 ratio of TRE3G‑hETV2‑EGFP‑EF1α‑TETOn3G‑PuroR and EF1α‑PB‑amp) in 25 µL Opti‑MEM; (c) Combine tubes, gently resuspend and incubate 15 min at 20‑22 °C.
Add 50 µL of the transfection mixture dropwise to each well, swirl gently for even distribution, and incubate 24 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.
Refresh E8 medium the next day and then daily for at least 5 days to allow puromycin‑resistance expression.
After 5 days, select transfected cells by incubating 24 h in E8 (or E8 Flex) containing 2 µg/mL puromycin (adjust based on a pre‑determined puromycin survival curve).
Repeat puromycin selection 3–4 days later for an additional 24 h to obtain a pure population of ETV2‑expressing iPSCs.
Pause point: Create a single‑cell suspension, freeze 1 × 10⁶ cells in 1 mL E8 Flex supplemented with 10 µM Y‑27632 and 10 % DMSO, and store at –150 °C.

steps.title: Immunostain induced endothelial cells
steps.instruction: Fix, permeabilize, block, and label iECs with primary and secondary antibodies for fluorescence imaging.

substeps.instruction: Fix cells in each well of an 8‑well chamber with 400 µL 4 % formaldehyde in PBS (20‑22 °C) for 15 min.
Wash 3 ×  with 400 µL PBS, 5 min each wash.
Optional: Store fixed cells in PBS at 4 °C until further processing.
Permeabilize with 400 µL 0.1 % Triton X‑100 in PBS for 5 min.
Wash once with 400 µL PBS.
Block with 400 µL 3 % BSA in PBS for 30 min at room temperature.
Add 120 µL of primary antibody diluted in 3 % BSA/PBS blocking buffer; incubate 10–18 h in a humid chamber at 4 °C.
Wash 3 ×  with 400 µL PBS.
Add 120 µL of fluorophore‑conjugated secondary antibody diluted in 3 % BSA/PBS; incubate 1 h at 20‑22 °C (alternatively 10–16 h at 4 °C).
Wash 3 ×  with 400 µL PBS.
Optional: Incubate with 200 µL DAPI (5 µg/mL) for 5 min for nuclear staining.
Wash once with 400 µL PBS.
Mount coverslips with Fluoromount‑G (or similar) and store at 4 °C in the dark until imaging.
Image using an epifluorescence or confocal microscope (20×, 40× or 63× objectives).

steps.title: Immunostain brain‑slice co‑culture
steps.instruction: Fix, detach, block, and label ex‑vivo mouse brain explants co‑cultured with iPSC‑derived iECs.

substeps.instruction: After 48 h of co‑culture, gently remove medium from the bottom of each transwell insert with a pipette (do not use vacuum).
Fix the explant by adding 350 µL 4 % formaldehyde per 12‑well insert (both on top of the slice and in the well bottom) and incubate 1 h at 20‑22 °C.
Remove fixative and wash the slice 3 ×  with 350 µL PBS, 5 min each wash.

Detach the membrane containing the slice with a scalpel, then transfer the free‑floating slice into a well of a 24‑well plate containing PBS. If the slice adheres to the membrane, gently shake or use a metal spatula.
Block the tissue with 500 µL brain‑slice blocking buffer for 1 h at 20‑22 °C.
Incubate with primary antibodies diluted in 200 µL antibody‑dilution buffer for brain slices; shake gently and incubate 10–18 h at 4 °C.
Wash 5 ×  with 500 µL PBS + 0.25 % Triton X‑100, 10 min each at 20‑22 °C.
Add secondary antibodies diluted in 200 µL antibody‑dilution buffer; incubate 3 h at 20‑22 °C with gentle shaking.
Wash 5 ×  with 500 µL PBS + 0.25 % Triton X‑100, 10 min each at 20‑22 °C.
Using a curved spatula, transfer the slice onto a glass slide (add a drop of PBS to aid transfer) and remove excess PBS.
Mount the slice between two coverslips (or place the slice on a slide with the cell‑applied side facing the coverslip) using Fluoromount‑G; apply gentle pressure to flatten.
Let the mounted slides dry at 4 °C, then image with a confocal microscope (20× or 40× objectives).

steps.title: Image analysis and statistics
steps.instruction: Convert images, quantify fluorescence and vasculature, and perform statistical analysis.

substeps.instruction: Export all fluorescence or confocal images as TIFF files using ImageJ.
For iEC marker assessment, open TIFFs in LAS X for qualitative inspection, then quantify intensity and distribution with CellProfiler.

For brain‑slice vasculature, upload TIFFs to REAVER (or similar MATLAB‑based software). Select the vascular channel, run “segment image”, skeletonize, and adjust the grey‑threshold manually if needed; add or remove segments to refine segmentation.
Run “Quantify all images” in REAVER to obtain metrics such as vessel_area_fraction, branchpoint_count, mean_segment_length_um, and mean_segment_diam_um.
Compile quantitative data and analyze using GraphPad Prism (or equivalent). Include at least three biological replicates per condition and apply appropriate statistical tests.
